articles.title: Ethiopia: Who could bring the warring sides to the negotiation table?

paras.en: Just four years after a landmark peace deal officially halted the devastating Tigray war, fighting has escalated once again in northern Ethiopia in recent weeks.

Just days before full-scale fighting resumed, several armed groups which had previously considered each enemies formally announced an alliance with a common goal: To bring down Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's federal government.

But this time, the lay of the land looks quite different from the previous conflict: Parties outside the country have been accused of meddling in the situation, with each having their own motives to want to destabilize Abiy's government.
This has raised fears about prolonged instability hitting the Horn of Africa.
Reasons for the collapse of the peace deal

The 2022 Pretoria Peace Agreement ended the conflict between the Ethiopian federal government and the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), which cost hundreds of thousands of lives in the course of two years.

Negash Mohammed, a journalist with DW's Amharic department. believes that the deal collapsed for three key reasons — or rather because three key actors in the conflict were largely neglected at the negotiation table.

Mohammed explained that the ultimate agreement didn't factor in the role of Eritrea in the conflict, which had fought alongside Ethiopia against the TPLF; it ignored the part that Amhara militias — known as Fano — played in the war, who later felt sorely excluded from the negotiations; finally, it ignored harliners within the TPLF who viewed the peace peace as nothing but military defeat.
Tensions between the federal government and the Fano escalated further when Addis Ababa moved to forcibly disarm the militias instead of addressing their grievances.
"The federal government has its own shortcomings," said Mohammed. "Instead of convincing the other side, it went on to aggravate the grievances they [already] had."
Mohammed also emphasized the fact that this coalition against the federal government includes several groups which have otherwise little to do with each other.

It includes the Oromo Liberation Army, a faction of the Ogaden National Liberation Front as well as multiple smaller armed groups from the western Benishangul-Gumuz region — in addition to ethnic militant factions from Afar, which borders Tigray.
Eritrea meanwhile appears to have shifted sides in the current situation: While not officially a member of the alliance, the neighboring country is believed to be providing support to the rebels.

Patricia Rodrigues, a senior analyst at Control Risks, a global intelligence and security consultancy, referred to the level of strategic coordination among these various groups in the current conflict as "quite significant" and "definitely alarming for the federal government."

She noted, however, that cracks might eventually appear: "How long this coalition lasts, because all of them have very different interests and represent very different ethnic constituencies, remains to be seen," she told DW.

Rodrigues added that, based on Control Risks' assessment, the fighting is likely to remain limited to Ethiopia's northern regions, particularly those situated along the borders between Tigray, Amhara, and Afar.

Furthermore, she highlighted that the idea of it spreading across the entire country was rather unlikely due to the difficulty of nationwide coordination, taking into consideration the rough terrain of the nation and the fragmentation of other opposition groups.
Rodrigues also pointed out the failure of sustained international engagement after the end of the crisis in 2022 as a key reason for the current conflict_

She noted that while the Pretoria agreement saw some early proof of implementation — including the TPLF's surrender of heavy weaponry in 2022 and 2023 — international attention had soon shifted to other global crises, leaving both sides free to quietly rearm and conscript supporters.
"It was more of a stopgap or a ceasefire, but people were quickly rearming in the background," she told DW.

Rodrigues also noted that the United States had recently lifted sanctions imposed during the 2020–2022 conflict — a step which, according to Mohammed, diminishes the West's leverage in the conflict to push combatants toward coming to the negotiation table.

In the meantime, civilians are bearing the cost of the warring parties: People caught up in the crossfire have been fleeing the conflict once more, adding further to a population of internally displaced persons (IDPs) that has not recovered from the previous war.

"Since 2020, they have not returned to their areas. They are still in makeshift IDP centers," Mohammed said, adding that there have also been isolated reports of drone strikes hitting civilian areas and of rebel groups deploying military hardware inside schools and clinics.

Telephone and internet connections have also been cut in parts of Tigray and Amhara, electricity has been disrupted, and flights have been suspended to several cities including Kombolcha and Lalibela.
Despite official assurances from all parties that civilians would be protected, Mohammed says that the reality on the ground tells a different story: "Words and practice are very contradictory."

Mohammed also noted that outgoing UN Secretary-General António Guterres dispatched a special envoy to the Horn of Africa, charged with mediating between the African Union, regional powers, and Egypt — many of the same parties involved in brokering the Pretoria agreement.

However according to Mohammed, meaningful negotiations are unlikely to bear fruit until at least one of the sides involved in the conflict "comes to understand that this violence will not help them to achieve what they want."

Rodrigues agrees, stressing that she cannot be optimistic about "an international or a regional mediation being the solution to the current fighting," adding that "intense, but geographically contained" fighting will continue for the foreseeable future.
Adapted from the AfricaLink Podcast by Silja Fröhlich

articles.title: Despite praise and White House visits, Trump avoids endorsing Netanyahu

paras.en: United States President Donald Trump has avoided directly endorsing Benjamin Netanyahu in an interview ahead of Israel’s upcoming elections, despite repeatedly heaping praise – and White House visits – on the Israeli prime minister.
Trump thrice avoided making an endorsement in an interview with Time magazine published on Thursday, instead pivoting to his own popularity in Israel and actions in support of Israel’s government.
- list 1 of 3Israel’s Netanyahu criticises opposition uniting against him for elections
- list 2 of 3Trump administration ‘must be changed’: Iran’s IRGC appeals to US voters
- list 3 of 3The October 7 warnings threatening Netanyahu’s Israeli election campaign
The US president was initially asked if the “Israeli people should give Netanyahu another term?”
“Well, I can only say that I’m not involved in politics any more, except that we’re popular,” Trump said, claiming “99 percent” popularity in Israel.

When pressed a second time on whether Netanyahu should have another term, Trump pointed to Washington’s continued security support for Israel and his decision to move the US embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem during his first term.
The interviewer responded: “It seems like you’re doing a lot of work for him. Should he have another term?”

Trump replied: “No, my primary thing – I do want to help them defend Israel. My thing that I mention all the time is Iran cannot have a nuclear power because they are crazy and you can’t let crazy people have nuclear weapons.”
Trump has repeatedly hailed his relationship with Netanyahu throughout his second term, even as government officials have leaked accounts of private discord between the two leaders.
Trump has met with Netanyahu at least seven times since January 2025, more than any other leader, and has publicly pushed for a pardon in the Israeli leader’s ongoing corruption trial.

Still, the latest statements come as Trump and his Republican Party have contended with growing discontent with his administration’s policy towards Israel, particularly amid perceptions that the Israeli government influenced Trump to launch the US-Israel war against Iran in February.

The conflict, which has driven up petrol prices in the US, has become a key vulnerability ahead of the US midterm elections in November, which will determine whether Democrats or Republicans control the US Senate and House of Representatives for Trump’s final two years in office.

Nevertheless, Trump hosted Netanyahu most recently at the White House in July, flouting concerns over Israeli obstructions to ending the conflict, as well as to achieving a more lasting peace in Israel’s genocidal war in Gaza.
Speaking to Time magazine, Trump defended the war with Iran, saying he may still seek to “annihilate” Iran and could resume bombing after the midterm vote.
Trump also came to Netanyahu’s defence, batting away reports that Egypt and the United Arab Emirates had warned Netanyahu of the impending Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel on October 7, 2023.
“I think if he would have known, he would have done something about it,” he said.
He later acknowledged that “people have written off Bibi many, many times, just like they’ve written off me many, many times”, using Netanyahu’s nickname.
“I wouldn’t underestimate Bibi,” he added.
Trump was also asked if US security support would change if Gadi Eisenkot, whose opposition bloc has been leading in Israeli polls, were to win the October 27 vote.
He replied: “Well, I don’t know. I don’t hear bad things about him.”

articles.title: Renee Good’s family sues Trump administration over fatal ICE shooting

paras.en: The family of Renee Good, one of two US citizens fatally shot by federal immigration agents in the state of Minnesota, has sued the government over her killing during a sweeping immigrant deportation blitz in January.

The two lawsuits – filed on Thursday by Good’s partner, Becca Good, and Renee’s brother, Brent Ganger – say officials from US President Donald Trump’s administration were reckless and violated the civil rights of Good and others in Minneapolis. The lawsuits are demanding a jury trial and financial damages.
The lawsuits are the first major civil actions taken against the Trump administration over its unprecedented deportation crackdowns in Minneapolis last winter, dubbed Operation Metro Surge.
The first lawsuit seeks damages for Good’s wrongful death under Minnesota law, citing claims of assault, battery, false imprisonment, negligence and intentional infliction of emotional distress.

The second lawsuit alleges a civil rights conspiracy among numerous defendants including the immigration officer and shooter Jonathon Ross, who was named alongside high-ranking Trump administration officials, including White House Deputy Policy Chief Stephen Miller, former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, former Border Patrol commander Gregory Bovino and Trump’s longtime campaign adviser, Corey Lewandowski.

Good, a mother of three, was shot and killed in her car by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent in south Minneapolis when she and her wife joined one of the city’s daily demonstrations against masked and armed federal agents deployed to the city to arrest migrants for deportation.
Widespread cellphone footage taken by eyewitnesses captured the moment in which Good was killed, after agent Ross fired into the windshield, shooting her in the head, arm and torso.
Federal officials at the time said the officer acted in self-defence and that Good had engaged in “an act of domestic terrorism”.

In a statement posted on Truth Social at the time, Trump defended the deadly ICE shooting, saying that the reason those “incidents” were happening was that “the Radical Left is threatening, assaulting, and targeting our Law Enforcement Officers and ICE Agents on a daily basis”.

Days after the shooting, officials from the US Department of Justice, including then-Deputy Attorney Todd Blanche, blocked federal prosecutors from pursuing a criminal civil rights case against the agents involved in her killing, which prompted at least half a dozen of those prosecutors to resign in protest.

Minnesota sued the Trump administration in March to gain access to the evidence it gathered at the shooting scenes, but investigations stalled after the Justice Department halted its routine cooperation and evidence-sharing with the Minneapolis Police Department.
None of the agents involved in Good’s killing has faced any charges.

articles.title: US Supreme Court agrees to take up Trump’s ICE detention policy

paras.en: The United States Supreme Court has agreed to hear a case focused on the Trump administration’s policy requiring millions of undocumented immigrants to remain in detention while they fight deportation.
The case, accepted on Thursday by the justices, is the latest dispute over US President Donald Trump’s sweeping immigration crackdown to reach the nation’s highest court.
- list 1 of 3US citizen injured after wrongly arrested by ICE in Illinois
- list 2 of 3Venezuelan man shot by ICE officer in Texas is charged with assault
- list 3 of 3US judge rules Wisconsin mosque leader Salah Sarsour can be deported

At issue is whether migrants already living in the US have a legal right to a hearing where a judge can decide whether they should be released on bond from Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention while their deportation cases are pending.

In July 2025, the administration introduced new guidance directing federal immigration authorities to detain undocumented immigrants without a bond hearing for the duration of their deportation proceedings, which can last for years.

The new policy, which has divided lower courts, reverses a decades-old interpretation that allowed some immigrants in the US to be released while their cases were pending in immigration court, according to Reuters news agency.

Most US federal appeals courts have ruled that immigrants cannot be detained without a bond hearing. But the 5th and 8th US Circuit Courts of Appeals have found that immigrants accused of illegally entering and remaining in the country must remain detained while their deportation cases proceed.
Trump administration attorneys told the Associated Press the split is “disrupting the orderly administration of immigration law”.

“The result is an unworkable patchwork of inconsistent immigration enforcement, where aliens present without admission are subject to mandatory detention in some circuits but are entitled to bond hearings and often released in others,” the lawyers wrote.
The Supreme Court case stems from a 2nd US Circuit Court of Appeals ruling involving Ricardo Aparecido Barbosa da Cunha, a Brazilian national who entered the US around 2004 or 2005.

Immigration officers arrested him in September 2025 while he was driving to work in the US state of Massachusetts. He was initially denied a bond hearing under the administration’s policy but was later released on bond, according to court documents cited by Reuters.

The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), which is representing the plaintiffs, told the Associated Press the Trump administration is trying to deny bond hearings for immigrants apprehended within the US rather than limiting the restriction to noncitizens stopped at the border.
“Millions of noncitizens could be affected by the government’s new interpretation,” ACLU attorneys wrote.
The Supreme Court is expected to hear arguments on Monday, when its new term starts.

articles.title: Picanha, prices and politics: What Brazil's favorite steak says about the election
articles.author: Catherine Osborn

paras.en: Picanha, prices and politics: What Brazil's favorite steak says about the election

RIO DE JANEIRO — As Brazilians prepare to vote in the first round of the presidential election Sunday, they're weighing sharp differences between the top candidates on security, foreign policy and the environment. But they're also thinking about kitchen table issues.
And if you really want to know how Brazilians feel about the economy, look no further than how often picanha, the country's prized cut of beef, is on the table.

When left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was campaigning for his current role four years ago, he told voters they would be able to afford picanha again if he were elected. At the time, Brazil's economy was still recovering from the COVID-19 pandemic.
Picanha, or a top sirloin cap steak, is a marker of prosperity in this beef-loving country.

Lula is now running for reelection in what polls suggest is a tight race with Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro. Lula's economic record is among the many issues under scrutiny by voters — and a recent survey found that only 10% of Brazilians feel their income has grown faster than the cost of living in the past year.

Marcella Pirozzi, 44, the co-owner of a Rio de Janeiro barbecue company, says these days she only tries to sell picanha in wealthy parts of the city. In poorer areas, people are "more conservative" about their spending, she says. "We don't get hired to cater events very often due to meat prices."

At his butcher shop on Rio's working-class north side, 37-year-old Arthur Guedes says he's also scaled back how much picanha he expects to sell in recent years. Instead, he's focusing on a more accessible product: hamburger patties.

After Lula took office, a burst of public spending caused economic growth to speed up, though it's now slowing. In the first three years of his term, average wages grew more than inflation. But household indebtedness also shot up, thanks to factors like a boom in sports gambling, easy access to credit lines, and high interest rates.
By this June, Brazilian households were spending 26.6% of their income on non-mortgage debt payments, according to the central bank.

Some analysts say a concept from the United States now applies in Brazil: that of a "vibecession." The term was first used in former President Joe Biden's administration to describe an economy that is not technically in recession, but feels unaffordable.

University of São Paulo economist Laura Carvalho argues the phrase is apt. She says the gap between the economic data and how it's perceived could come from Brazilians making mental comparisons with an earlier period when Lula was president, in the 2000s. Brazil's economy boomed dramatically, and many families could afford items like refrigerators and air travel for the first time.

In contrast, today's economy is suffering from price shocks that didn't exist back then, Carvalho said: "the pandemic, and then the war in Ukraine, and now, with the Iran war." Trump's heavy tariffs on Brazil have also taken an economic toll.
Brazil's voter worries about the cost of living are part of a worldwide phenomenon, according to Carvalho.
"You have incumbents everywhere that are suffering the effects of the price increases of the different shocks," she said. "People look at the price increase and they blame whoever is in government."

Bolsonaro, a senator for Rio de Janeiro, is playing up the idea that basic staples have become unaffordable. He published a video of himself denouncing prices in the supermarket, making sure to name-check picanha.

But he has not given much detail about his own economic proposals. He broadly argues that cutting taxes and government spending will boost growth. One of Bolsonaro's top advisers has praised the policies of libertarian Argentine President Javier Milei, which have reduced inflation but seen poverty rise in recent months.

Lula, for his part, has downplayed concerns that Brazil's national debt might be getting unsustainable. He's announced new measures in recent days meant to address household indebtedness, like a debt restructuring program and ban on online betting.
Guedes, the butcher shop owner, says that only days before the election, he still hasn't decided how to vote.
"I don't see clear strategies from the candidates for how to improve the country," he says.
Pirozzi has made up her mind. She says she's "ready for a change" and will vote for Bolsonaro.

articles.title: Passengers recount chaos on Tel Aviv flight. And, FBI probes employee-data hack
articles.author: Brittney Melton

paras.en: Passengers recount chaos on Tel Aviv flight. And, FBI probes employee-data hack

A flydubai plane headed to Tel Aviv yesterday made an emergency landing after one pilot stabbed the other in a possible attempt to crash the plane. Most of the roughly 170 passengers were Israeli. Some passengers entered the cockpit and subdued the attacker after the injured pilot unlocked the door. Another flight crew on board then helped land the plane safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The motive remains unknown.

- 🎧 NPR's Kat Lonsdorf was at the Tel Aviv airport as passengers returned. She tells Up First the arrivals area was packed with journalists and family members as passengers came through: some crying, some smiling and many looking exhausted. One passenger told Lonsdorf he tried to keep his young son calm during the ordeal. Another, a plumber, said he helped subdue the attacker and pulled up on the plane's controls after remembering something he had seen on TV. The incident comes less than a month before Israel's national election and is likely to become part of the campaign conversation in the weeks ahead.

U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth says he wants fewer generals and admirals — and a military built around drones, AI and what he calls a "warrior ethos." In a speech at Quantico yesterday, Hegseth said he has already cut the number of senior officers by about 10% and wants to reach 20%. He also announced a new military command focused on drones and other emerging technologies, even as the U.S. remains at war with Iran.

- 🎧 NPR's Quil Lawrence says the issue is less about shrinking the top ranks than about who Hegseth is removing and why. Hegseth has blocked some colonels from becoming generals without publicly explaining the decisions and has fired several senior officers. Lawrence also notes that the Pentagon has not held a news briefing since May, which is a stark contrast to the previous two decades of sometimes intense warfare in Iraq and Afghanistan.

The FBI says it is "aggressively" investigating a cyberattack claimed by ShinyHunters after the group said it stole sensitive FBI employment data. It is still unclear how much information was taken or whether hackers got in through third-party software or the bureau's own systems. Some current and former employees told NPR the stolen files may include job applications, promotion records, family details and medical information.

President Trump is traveling to Oklahoma today — not a battleground state but a place where he can test-drive his midterm message with a friendly crowd. Trump promised to campaign for Republicans in 35 competitive races, but his first stops are in reliably red states like Oklahoma and Alabama.

- 🎧 NPR's Franco Ordoñez says that the trips are partly about energizing voters who reliably turn out for Trump but may be harder to motivate when he isn't on the ballot. Oklahoma also gives Trump a lower-risk place to try out campaign lines before heading to more competitive states, where his presence could just as easily motivate Democrats and independents.

The U.S. has drawn heavily from its Strategic Petroleum Reserve since the war with Iran began, shrinking the stockpile by more than 30% in six months. The reserve, stored in underground salt caverns in Louisiana and Texas, is one of the government's main tools for easing pressure on gas prices. Here's what to know:
- 🛢️ Rapid drawdowns can damage the reserve itself, putting stress on the salt caverns and other infrastructure.
- 🛢️ The Trump administration is exploring a possible oil swap with Venezuela, though much of the crude under discussion is heavy and difficult to extract.
- 🛢️ China has also tapped its reserves, but less aggressively as electric vehicles make up a larger share of transportation there.
by Geoff Brumfiel, NPR's senior editor and correspondent
OpenAI says its AI helped solve one of math's hardest problems. The catch? Mathematicians weren't quite sure how it got there.

That's what I discovered when I started talking to mathematicians about what was supposed to be one of the biggest discoveries this century. It turned out OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra model was not some machine supergod that outstripped human intellect – it was just that it was really bad at showing its work.

Suddenly, a very abstruse and vague math story felt pretty relatable. Who hasn't been scolded by a teacher for skipping the steps? And who hasn't gotten an AI answer that sounds impressive but leaves you wondering what on earth it just said?

Mathematicians believe the answer is correct, but the AI-generated proof runs 166 pages, and they say it may take weeks to untangle what actually matters. Despite the lack of clarity, they're excited about the possibility of using AI to solve more problems in the future.

articles.title: What a Pearly King taught me about Cockney rhyming slang and East London history
articles.author: Lauren Frayer

paras.en: What a Pearly King taught me about Cockney rhyming slang and East London history
LONDON — He was one of my most memorable interviews. Even though we were both speaking English, I could barely understand a word he was saying.
"The costermongers, wheeze used to fly-pitch, on this frog and toad," he said — at least I think, after listening to my tape several times again, none the wiser.

Our interview was back in 2016, on one of my first NPR reporting trips to London. George Major, then 78, was a local celebrity. We walked together through the East End, where the factories and docklands that Major grew up around during World War II have given way to glass skyscrapers. A vendor ran out into the street to slap him high-five. Tourists snapped photos.

Major had turned up in bling: A black suit and flat cap, both festooned with sequins, sparkles and mother-of-pearl buttons. His title — Pearly King of Peckham — was spelled out in shimmering buttons across the back of his jacket.
He was a charming wheeler-dealer. But his language — a mix of what he called "backspeak" and Cockney rhyming slang — was impossible for this hapless American visitor to understand.
At one point in our video interview, I glanced at the camera and exclaimed, "We might need a translator here!"

Ten years later, I chuckle whenever I land at Heathrow Airport, where a portrait of Major covers an entire wall. But this summer, a former colleague alerted me to an item in the local press, which hit me harder than I expected: The Pearly King of Peckham died Aug. 1, aged 88.

He was buried Sept. 14 in a cemetery not far from the Cockney Museum he founded. A horse-drawn cart carried his casket into a little chapel, whose walls shook with mourners singing raucous pub songs. One of the gardeners outside looked bewildered.
At the gravesite, I approached the Major family, offered condolences, and hesitantly shared the story of my brief, confusing 2016 encounter with their loved one.

A horde of pearly kings, queens, princes and princesses — four generations of Major's family, all in matching pearly suits — turned and looked at me, some through tears, then threw back their heads and laughed.
"A real Cockney cheeky chappy!" his daughter Janet Major said, hugging me.

In the 1870s, an orphaned street sweeper named Henry Croft began decorating his suit with mother-of-pearl buttons scavenged from the streets outside textile factories that used to dot London's East End.
His pearly garb infused menial work with dignity — a royal air, even — and launched what would become a working-class East London institution: The pearly kings and queens.

"These pearly suits are now cultural artifacts with fantastic designs, telling a profound story about London and Cockneys, what we call the non-posh Londoners," says Andy Green, co-founder of the Modern Cockney Festival, an annual celebration of diverse, working-class communities in London.

Some of the so-called pearlies were street hawkers, market vendors or fly-pitchers — unlicensed traders. Others canvassed for charity. Many were immigrants, their slang peppered with words from Yiddish or Bengali. They became neighborhood fixtures, in mother-of-pearl finery.

"You had what are called costermongers, which is a posh word for street hawkers, street sellers," Green says. "Imagine you're a newly arrived immigrant in the country. One of the first jobs you could possibly do might be to hustle, sell goods on the street."

That's what George Major did. Born in 1938 inside a military barracks in Peckham, southeast London, he was abandoned as a child, grew up in a workhouse, and found odd jobs in the local market as a teenager, his daughter Janet explains.

"Dad eventually became one of the costermonger kings that used to run market stalls," she says. "It was not an easy childhood, but he followed the ideals of Henry Croft. That was before the welfare state, when you had to help your friends, your neighbors, your community."
Janet Major describes the weekends of her childhood, with her father leading all seven of his children, walking door to door in matching pearly suits, asking for money for charity.
Nowadays, a dwindling number of pearlies still canvass for charities like children's hospitals, women's shelters and veterans groups. They appear at summertime street festivals and march in parades.
George Major later trained as a plumber and ran a plumbing supply shop, she says.

Onscreen, the pearly kings inspired the streetwise, heart-of-gold chimney sweep character of Bert in Walt Disney's Mary Poppins film — played by Dick Van Dyke, an American who later owned up to what he called "the most atrocious Cockney accent in the history of cinema."

The Major family and others believe George Major himself inspired another fictional character: Del Boy, the happy-go-lucky East London huckster in the long-running British sitcom Only Fools and Horses. He's a cheeky salesman, always scheming to get rich quick, with the catchphrase, "This time next year, we'll be millionaires!"
At his funeral, Major's eulogy was riddled with Del Boy quotes.
But like the TV protagonist, Major also broke the law. In 2012 he was sentenced to six months in prison, after pleading guilty to benefits fraud. He was released early.
"If he could avoid the tax man, he would!" his daughter laughs. "He used to say, 'Discount for cash!' He'd love a bargain."
His fame overshadowed his legal troubles. Major was one of dozens of pearly royals who marched in the opening ceremony of the 2012 London Olympics.

Years later, I finally figured out what Major meant back in 2016 when he told me he was a "costermonger" (street hawker) who used to "fly-pitch" (sell stuff without a license) on the "frog and toad" where we did our interview.

In Cockney rhyming slang, "frog and toad" means road. "Porky pies" means lies. "Apples and pears" means stairs. "Whistle and flute" means suit. "Ruby Murray" means curry. The vocabulary is extensive, and bewildering to outsiders — which is precisely the point. Green, the Cockney expert, says this type of slang likely originated as a code to confuse the police, or to secretly rig prices among street vendors.

To complicate things, Major also spoke in what he called "backspeak," sometimes also called backslang, which is even more confusing. One example that's crept into mainstream British slang is the word "yob" for boy. Take any word at all, and simply spell it backwards.

One of the only parts of that 2016 interview I could understand at the time was when Major waxed poetic about his family's unique pearly suit pattern. He pointed to a row of buttons on his sleeve, calling them "the line of life."
Ten years later, at his funeral, I found myself examining the same pattern on a pearly outfit worn by his great-granddaughter.

"There's a straight line, which is your life line," Aleisha Gordon, 19, said, pointing to a row of shimmering buttons. "The triangles are the ups and downs in life, and the flowers are the friends and family that help you along the way."

After the funeral, children threw handfuls of earth as George Major's coffin was lowered into the ground. The undertaker brought out four caged doves for Major's descendants to release skyward. The birds circled twice overhead, then disappeared.

People shared anecdotes about a "real rascal" and "the most hilarious person" who was nevertheless "very particular" about who made his tea. Someone turned on a boombox, and mourners began kicking their legs like the can-can, singing along to 1950s songs.
They paraded out of the cemetery toward a nearby nuclear sub — what Cockneys call the pub — for a cool pint of pig's ear, or King Lear.
At least that's what the Pearly King of Peckham would have called it. Now I finally understand.

They did get a bit lucky that there was a lightning strike that stopped Tampa's momentum late in the game. articles.title: Jayden Daniels does not dismiss playing Sunday against the Colts in London after ugly elbow dislocation injury

paras.en: Jayden Daniels' journey through his elbow dislocation 11 days ago has been a rollercoaster ride, especially if you saw how the injury happened, and the concern that it ended his season prematurely. But we've reached the point where the Washington Commanders quarterback is talking to the media again and even suggesting he might play on Sunday.

Daniels, in London with his teammates for the game against the Indianapolis Colts, faced reporters for the first time since his injury on Sept. 20 and was almost immediately asked if he could play this week.
"It feels good," Daniels said of his left elbow, which was also dislocated last season. "Feels good to be back and, you know, taking it day by day."
Daniels has practiced the past two days to varying degrees. Is he surprised that he's been able to get back on the field this soon?

"What you think?" Daniels playfully responded to the question. "I'm not surprised. No, everything I went through, you know, everybody said, I'd be good to go if I'm able to go out there on Sunday, but again, just taking it day by day."
So, um, the money question: Is he indeed playing on Sunday?
" Just taking the day by day," he replied.
COMMANDERS PLAYERS PUSH BACK ON THE NARRATIVE THEY DIDN'T CARE ABOUT JAYDEN DANIELS INJURY
Looking for a no, in that response. Not there.
In fact, a source close to Daniels told OutKick that while he is "not pushing coaches" to play on Sunday, that is exactly what he wants to do.

But it's not ultimately his decision. Coach Dan Quinn on Wednesday said the team wants to gauge how Daniels looks in practices this week before making a final decision on whether to start backup Marcus Mariota or return Daniels to the lineup.

"As we're working through the week, he'll get more [repetitions in practice]," Quinn said. "It's part of our return-to-play process where guys do individual, that kind of limited portion, then some of the team reps and then more.
"As we get into Thursday and Friday, we'll see what that load looks like. And by Friday, we'll have a definite determination of where we're at."
Looking for the part where Quinn says Daniels is out. Not there.

It does not take Sherlock Holmes to figure out that while in London, the Commanders are sounding almost hopeful about their starting quarterback's status. And part of that is leaving the door ajar for his return this week.
This is a bit surprising because in the days after the elbow injury, there was a real possibility Daniels could require surgery and be out the remainder of the season.

Then Daniels met with multiple medical experts and decided wearing a brace, while affecting the functionality to his non-throwing arm, would be acceptable. His return to play is not a pain tolerance issue.
So, Daniels decided to return – be that this week or the next, barring a setback.

"I love football. I play football," Daniels said in explaining his reason for returning. "I mean, I get paid to play football, so, I went to my teammates and stuff like that to see that everybody's hurting. Something's wrong with everybody on this team.
"So, I just feel like just for me, just being a leader, being a guy, just going out there and, give it my shot to go out there and play and obviously protect myself, you know, stuff like that.
"But, you know, I just love football. I have a passion for it."

articles.title: Britain in talks with European allies over release of emergency diesel stockpiles
articles.author: Alex Daniel

paras.en: Britain is in talks with European allies over releasing emergency diesel stockpiles after Donald Trump threatened to cut off US supplies of the fuel.

Ministers held calls with counterparts from the European Commission, Germany, France, Italy and Ireland on Thursday to discuss whether to draw down reserves after the Trump administration told Germany and France to release their stockpiles to help ease soaring global energy prices or face a US export ban.

The warning, first reported by Reuters, marks an escalation of pressure on Europe as Trump considers a potential wider ban to help lower domestic fuel prices before the US midterm elections in November.

A US official told the news agency: “It is in Europe’s best interest to work with the United States as we pursue multiple pathways to boost the supply of refined products and lower costs for consumers.”
Martin McCluskey, the UK minister for local energy, was reportedly on the call with EU countries on Thursday.
The Trump administration has been frustrated with France and Germany for what it considers their not following through on commitments to release oil and petrol stocks.

Fuel stations across Europe are unlikely to run dry, because Europe produces about 70% of the diesel it consumes from domestic refineries. It also stores fuels in reserve. But experts fear that competing for cargoes on the global market would lead to higher market prices.

It was unclear whether the UK would be included in such a ban, but the loss of US supply would drive prices up sharply at the pumps because the UK does not refine enough diesel to meet domestic demand. About a third of UK diesel imports last year came from the US.
The average price of a litre of diesel in the UK hit a new all-time high on Wednesday of 199.72p, according to the motoring body the RAC.
John Healey, the chancellor, admitted earlier this week that UK diesel prices were “extreme” and said the government was in discussion with the US over trying to stop a ban.

The US war in Iran has disrupted energy supplies via the strait of Hormuz and sent the price of oil soaring. Before the war, in February, Brent crude – the international benchmark for oil prices – traded at about $72 a barrel. It was above $101 on Thursday.

Releasing more stocks would represent a problem for European countries, which need to balance the need to bring down domestic fuel prices with keeping high stocks for a potential worsening energy crisis over the winter if the Iran war continues.

“The UK continues to need fuels – from transport to chemicals, agriculture and defence,” said Elizabeth de Jong, the chief executive of the trade group Fuels Industry UK. The latest US threat showed the UK “cannot solely rely on overseas production for domestic energy security”, she added.

The US energy secretary, Chris Wright, said on Wednesday that the US administration expected announcements from Europe soon regarding new diesel supplies. “We’ve lost some diesel exports from the Middle East, although we’re restoring those, and we’ve lost diesel exports from China,” he said. “So that’s a lot of interruptions.”
Miatta Fahnbulleh, the UK energy secretary, has been in contact with Wright to raise concerns.

Trump has said he was “very seriously” considering a US diesel export ban to try to curb soaring prices, and has urged Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, to pause strikes on Russian oil refineries over concerns that they could further push up prices. Russia had already extended its ban on diesel exports until the end of October after Ukrainian attacks on refining companies.
A government spokesperson said: “We have a diverse and resilient supply. We continue to engage with our international partners and the UK fuel industry.”

articles.title: NAZA film-makers say they spoke to more than 100 sources about Israeli actions in Gaza
articles.author: Peter Beaumont

paras.en: The team behind the award-winning film NAZA, which details the Israeli military’s targeting policies in Gaza and its alleged acceptance of high numbers of civilian deaths, have revealed they spoke to more than 100 sources with knowledge of the military systems used in the war.
The disclosure came in response to an Israel Defense Forces statement seeking to discredit the documentary.

In its response, which the IDF said was based on statements made by the film-makers and a review made by a representative who had attended a viewing, the Israeli military claimed there were “substantial errors” in the film and that it had relied on interviews with two dozen intelligence and other troops who had only a partial picture of the target approval process.

At the centre of the IDF’s rebuttal was its often repeated claim that its rules of engagement explicitly distinguish between militants and civilians and prohibit deliberately targeting civilians, while requiring commanders to take steps to minimise civilian harm, claims that have long been challenged over the years by critics.
While acknowledging that it used AI to help recommend potential targets in Gaza, the IDF also said final decisions made on strikes, and the risk of civilian casualties, were signed off by officers.
The IDF also denied that it had approved, planned or carried out an attack anticipating 500 civilian casualties in pursuit of a single Hamas target.

The IDF statement follows previous efforts by Israeli politicians to dismiss NAZA – a military acronym euphemistically used by Israeli intelligence to indicate the number of civilians that it expects will be killed in an airstrike – which have accompanied death threats against the film’s directors, Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, and calls by the country’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, for them to be stripped of their Israeli citizenship.

It also echoed previous complaints by some Israeli critics – including journalists – that the film’s military sources were anonymised, despite the fact that source protection in media investigations is commonplace and regarded by much of the media as an ethical requirement.

“The film NAZA presents a distorted, misleading, and unrealistic picture of the IDF’s target planning and strike processes. The film’s narrative is based on fundamental factual errors stemming from a skewed and manipulative portrayal,” the statement added.

Responding to the IDF statement, the Guardian, which produced the film, disclosed further details of how the team had verified the allegations which involved scores of interviews with those with knowledge of IDF targeting and authorisation processes.
A spokesperson said: “The IDF’s attempt to portray the 24 participants in NAZA as junior-ranking officers involved only in the early stages of the targeting process is false.
“They include officers and soldiers who were involved in multiple stages of the targeting process in Gaza, including intelligence, operations and the final authorisation process.

“The process of assessing the credibility of the testimonies was rigorous. It included leaked classified documents, detailed verification of specific strikes and corroboration via a wider pool of confidential journalistic sources who did not appear on camera in the film.

“Over the past three years we have together interviewed more than 100 sources familiar with IDF systems used in the war in Gaza, including senior-ranking commanders directly involved in the authorisation of strikes.

“The Guardian stands fully behind the film, which builds on three years of detailed reporting by the Guardian and our partners. Several highly respected news organisations have subsequently confirmed the IDF’s use of AI-driven systems in the Gaza offensive and the loosening of safeguards to protect civilians, including the New York Times, Washington Post and Associated Press.”

While Netanyahu has claimed that Israeli military safeguards have led to one of the lowest civilian-combatant ratios in modern warfare, that has been challenged by the IDF’s own leaked casualty assessments, by the UN’s commission of inquiry in 2024 and research by NGOs including Action on Armed Violence.

articles.title: France school protests escalate into ‘urban violence’ as PM calls crisis cabinet meeting
articles.author: Jon Henley in Paris

paras.en: A fast-growing protest by high-school students over long hours, teacher shortages and decaying facilities has escalated into “urban violence”, the French government has warned, as it said many schools would switch to online classes to protect teachers and pupils.
paras.zh: 法国政府警告说，高中生长时间快速增长的抗议活动、教师短缺和设施腐烂已升级为“城市暴力” ，因为它表示许多学校将改用在线课程来保护教师和学生。

paras.en: The prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, called a crisis cabinet meeting on Thursday and told ministers to cancel travel plans to deal with the demonstrations, which erupted in the Paris region last week but have snowballed across the country.
paras.zh: 总理塞巴斯蒂安·勒科努（ Sébastien Lecornu ）周四召集了一次危机内阁会议，并告诉部长们取消应对示威活动的旅行计划，这些示威活动上周在巴黎地区爆发，但在全国各地滚雪球。

paras.en: Lecornu’s office said: “This upsurge in violence makes it virtually impossible to maintain the continuity of public education and is exposing staff and students to danger.” The education minister, Édouard Geffray, is to meet pupil representatives on Friday.
paras.zh: Lecornu的办公室说： “这种暴力的激增使得维持公共教育的连续性几乎不可能，并使工作人员和学生面临危险。“教育部长爱德华·杰弗里（ Édouard Geffray ）将于周五会见学生代表。

paras.en: About 900 demonstrations, blockades and related incidents were under way outside high schools around the country, police said, with more than 160 shut down as a result. Access was also blocked to about 30 university campuses on Thursday, including in Paris and Marseille.
paras.zh: 警方称，全国各地高中外发生约900起示威、封锁和相关事件，导致160多起关闭。周四，包括巴黎和马赛在内的大约30所大学校园也被封锁。

paras.en: Nearly 3,000 lycée students – aged between 15 and 18 – have been detained since the start of the protests, including 1,949 on Thursday alone, the interior ministry said. More than 300 police and dozens of firefighters, teachers and pupils have been injured.
paras.zh: 内政部表示，自抗议活动开始以来，已有近3000名15至18岁的学生被拘留，其中仅周四就有1949人被拘留。300多名警察和数十名消防员、教师和学生受伤。

paras.en: The pupils’ grievances range from overloaded timetables and overcrowded classes to insufficient teachers and unbearable temperatures during heatwaves earlier this year. Riot police have been deployed to confront the increasingly violent protests.
paras.zh: 学生的不满包括时间表超负荷和班级过度拥挤，以及今年早些时候热浪期间教师不足和难以忍受的温度。防暴警察已被部署以应对日益暴力的抗议活动。

paras.en: Injuries have mainly been from hurled objects but also from police-fired riot-control projectiles, with the interior ministry announcing an internal police investigation after accusations of excessive force and brutality by officers against three pupils.
paras.zh: 受伤主要来自投掷物体，但也来自警察发射的防暴射弹，内政部在指控警方对三名学生过度使用武力和残忍行为后宣布进行内部警方调查。

paras.en: Rubbish bins have been set on fire outside many schools and more serious arson attempts have been reported inside some buildings. Fire damage in one school in Nantes in the north-west was so extensive that it will stay closed for a month, authorities said.
paras.zh: 许多学校外面的垃圾桶被放火焚烧，据报道，一些建筑物内发生了更严重的纵火企图。当局表示，西北部南特一所学校的火灾损失如此之大，以至于它将关闭一个月。

paras.en: In the northern city of Caen, 16-year-old Maelle said she wished those setting bins on fire would protest “with words”. Students were protesting “against this government that doesn’t invest in heating, air conditioning, or teachers’ salaries”, she told AFP.
paras.zh: 在北部城市卡昂， 16岁的Maelle说，她希望那些放火烧垃圾桶的人能够“用言语”抗议。她告诉法新社，学生们正在抗议“这个不投资于供暖、空调或教师工资的政府”。

paras.en: In Strasbourg in the north-east, tram services were temporarily suspended to “restrict the movements of rioters and demonstrators”, the regional prefect said, after protesting students obstructed the tracks with crowd control barriers.
paras.zh: 这位地区省长说，在东北部的斯特拉斯堡，电车服务暂时停止，以“限制暴乱者和示威者的行动” ，此前抗议学生用人群控制屏障阻挡了轨道。

paras.en: “There are 35 of us per classroom,” one 17-year-old Strasbourg student said. “There aren’t enough toilets, and there are water leaks in some rooms. The building is falling apart, the cafeteria is too small. There’s zero budget, zero resources.”
paras.zh: 一位17岁的斯特拉斯堡学生说： “每个教室有35个人。”「厕所不够用，有些房间漏水。大楼正在倒塌，自助餐厅太小了。预算为零，资源为零。”

paras.en: Several bin fires were also reported in the southern city of Toulouse; while in Lille, young people wearing black hoodies destroyed a bus stop. In Marseille, there were attempts to light fires inside two schools. In one, a teacher was splashed with petrol.

While many teachers and several headteachers have reported being physically threatened and sometimes attacked, some support their pupils. Juliette Estiville, a high-school Spanish teacher in Paris, said that the police response had disgusted her.

“I’m actually here just to provide protection, to form a barrier between the police and the students,” she said. “Today went well, it’s going well, but I think that the teachers who come to the blockades are really there to protect our young people.”

The government has accused the radical left La France Insoumise (LFI) party of encouraging the protests, with several LFI MPs and mayors, including Bally Bagayoko, the LFI mayor of the Paris suburb of Saint-Denis, cheered at demonstrations.

The party’s candidate for the 2027 presidential election, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, insisted on Thursday that LFI backed “non-violent methods of struggle” and added that his “greatest worry is an unbearable level of police violence against these young people”.

articles.title: Putin warns West that Russia is ready to use every weapon to protect Kaliningrad

paras.en: Vladimir Putin has said Russia will use all weapons at his disposal if it considers it has come under direct attack in its Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad.
paras.zh: 弗拉基米尔·普京（ Vladimir Putin ）曾表示，如果俄罗斯认为在其波罗的海飞地加里宁格勒受到直接攻击，俄罗斯将使用他拥有的所有武器。

paras.en: Addressing the Valdai foreign policy forum, Putin insisted Russia was "not threatening anyone" and merely responding to statements by Western leaders that Moscow was preparing for war in 2029 or 2030.
paras.zh: 普京在瓦尔代外交政策论坛上发言时坚称，俄罗斯“没有威胁任何人” ，只是回应西方领导人的声明，称莫斯科正在为2029年或2030年的战争做准备。

paras.en: Throughout this week, Russia has accused Nato of preparing to blockade its territory, which borders Lithuania and Poland, warning that it would even be prepared to use nuclear weapons if the West tried to cut off Kaliningrad from the rest of Russia.
paras.zh: 本周，俄罗斯一直指责北约准备封锁其与立陶宛和波兰接壤的领土，并警告说，如果西方试图将加里宁格勒与俄罗斯其他地区隔离开来，它甚至会准备使用核武器。

paras.en: Nato has sought to calm the situation, stressing it is a defensive alliance and urging Moscow to stop its "nuclear threats".
paras.zh: 北约试图平息局势，强调这是一个防御联盟，并敦促莫斯科停止其“核威胁”。

paras.en: Western allies have faced a surge in so-called hybrid warfare incidents blamed on Russia, particularly in Poland and the Baltics in recent months.
paras.zh: 最近几个月，西方盟国面临着所谓的混合战争事件激增，这些事件归咎于俄罗斯，特别是在波兰和波罗的海国家。

paras.en: Last week alone Poland said a Russian helicopter had strayed into its territory adjacent to Kaliningrad and Lithuania said its population felt "constantly threatened" by Russia, in part because of drones entering the nation's airspace.
paras.zh: 仅上周，波兰就表示，一架俄罗斯直升机误入其毗邻加里宁格勒和立陶宛的领土，称其民众感到受到俄罗斯的“不断威胁” ，部分原因是无人机进入该国领空。

paras.en: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Thursday that his country was preparing for further hybrid attacks, "including serious ones", after a drone armed with explosives was found in August on the tarmac at Leipzig airport close to Ukrainian cargo planes.
paras.zh: 德国总理弗里德里希·默茨（ Friedrich Merz ）周四表示，在8月份在靠近乌克兰货机的莱比锡机场停机坪上发现一架携带爆炸物的无人机后，他的国家正在准备进一步的混合攻击， “包括严重的”。

paras.en: In a wide-ranging speech, the Russian leader told his audience he believed that international conflicts were highly likely to continue, but would get better as "Western hegemony" weakened.
paras.zh: 在一次范围广泛的演讲中，这位俄罗斯领导人告诉他的听众，他认为国际冲突极有可能继续下去，但随着“西方霸权”的削弱，情况会变得更好。

paras.en: Although Putin himself began the full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022, he again blamed the West for provoking the invasion, arguing that it had simply been forced to defend itself and take up arms.
paras.zh: 尽管普京本人于2022年2月在乌克兰发动了全面战争，但他再次指责西方挑起了入侵，认为它只是被迫自卫并拿起武器。

paras.en: He also insisted that Russia's attacks on Ukrainian economic targets were a direct response to Ukraine's strikes on Russia's oil refineries, and on its ships in the Black Sea.
paras.zh: 他还坚称，俄罗斯对乌克兰经济目标的攻击是对乌克兰对俄罗斯炼油厂及其在黑海船只的打击的直接回应。

paras.en: "Now from every direction we're receiving calls 'let's stop'. But they started it," he said.
paras.zh: “现在，我们从各个方向都接到了'让我们停下来'的电话。但他们开始了，”他说。

paras.en: Putin admitted Kyiv had "got some results" from its refinery attacks and Russia had lost about 1% of its GDP. Ukraine maintains it began attacking Russian oil infrastructure because it helped the Kremlin finance the war.
paras.zh: 普京承认，基辅从炼油厂袭击中“得到了一些结果” ，俄罗斯损失了约1 ％的国内生产总值。乌克兰坚称，它之所以开始攻击俄罗斯的石油基础设施，是因为它帮助克里姆林宫为这场战争提供了资金。

paras.en: Russia has targeted Ukrainian energy infrastructure, ramping up attacks every winter since the war on Ukraine started in 2022. Other civilian infrastructure is also regularly hit, and a key bridge in Kyiv was attacked by drones on Thursday.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯瞄准了乌克兰的能源基础设施，自2022年对乌克兰的战争开始以来，每年冬天都会加剧袭击。其他民用基础设施也经常受到袭击，周四，基辅的一座关键桥梁遭到无人机袭击。

paras.en: Putin also accused the West of instigating other conflicts.
paras.zh: 普京还指责西方煽动其他冲突。

paras.en: "If it comes to a direct attack on the Russian Federation, in this case we are talking about Kaliningrad but possibly some other territories, of course the issue of use by the Russian Federation of all arms at the disposal of our country will inevitably and immediately be on the agenda," he said.
paras.zh: 他说： “如果涉及对俄罗斯联邦的直接攻击，在这种情况下，我们谈论的是加里宁格勒，但可能还有其他一些领土，当然，俄罗斯联邦使用我们国家拥有的所有武器的问题将不可避免地立即列入议程。”

paras.en: He accused Nato of holding naval manoeuvres in the Baltic Sea which he argued represented serious threats to Kaliningrad. If the territory came under Western blockade, he said Russia would be prepared to use all means and forces, including nuclear.
paras.zh: 他指责北约在波罗的海举行海军演习，他认为这是对加里宁格勒的严重威胁。他表示，如果该领土受到西方封锁，俄罗斯将准备使用一切手段和力量，包括核武器。

paras.en: "We are not threatening anyone. We do not intend to attack anyone in 2029, in 2030, in 2050. But if we come across an aggression we will have to respond. Citizens of European countries should be fully aware of that."
paras.zh: “我们没有威胁任何人。我们不打算在2029年、2030年和2050年攻击任何人。但是，如果我们遇到侵略，我们将不得不做出回应。欧洲国家的公民应该充分意识到这一点。”

paras.en: He added that while he was aware of the nuclear capabilities of countries such as the UK and France, the weapons at its disposal were unparalleled.
paras.zh: 他补充说，虽然他知道英国和法国等国家的核能力，但其拥有的武器是无与伦比的。

paras.en: Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte made clear on Wednesday that none of the alliance's "exercises or activities" posed any threat to Moscow and the Kremlin's messaging was "absolutely not called for and not helpful".
paras.zh: 北约秘书长马克·吕特（ Mark Rutte ）周三明确表示，该联盟的任何“演习或活动”都没有对莫斯科构成任何威胁，克里姆林宫的信息“绝对没有必要，也没有帮助”。

paras.en: Putin spent some time talking about leading countries in the world having armaments at their disposal that could "swipe away all life or at least push the Earth to catastrophic consequences", and said unfortunately no-one could be sure they would never be used.
paras.zh: 普京花了一些时间谈论世界上主要国家拥有可以“摧毁所有生命或至少将地球推向灾难性后果”的军备，并表示不幸的是，没有人能确定它们永远不会被使用。

paras.en: He drew the analogy of a gun sitting on a theatre stage - if it was hanging there at the start of the show, it would certainly fire at the end.
paras.zh: 他画了一个比喻，一把枪坐在剧院的舞台上--如果它在演出开始时挂在那里，它肯定会在演出结束时开火。

paras.en: He appeared to call for the rules of warfare to be rewritten, and warned of the increasing risk of artificial intelligence.
paras.zh: 他似乎呼吁重写战争规则，并警告人工智能的风险越来越大。

paras.en: "The automation and digitalisation of warfare leads to its gamification. This leads to degradation and sliding back of humanity to barbarity," he said.
paras.zh: “战争的自动化和数字化导致其游戏化。这导致了人性的堕落和滑向野蛮，”他说。

articles.title: Netanyahu says Flydubai attacker had 'Islamist radical indoctrination'

paras.en: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says investigations suggest the man who stabbed his fellow pilot and tried to take over a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv had undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination".
paras.zh: 以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡（ Benjamin Netanyahu ）表示，调查表明，刺伤同伴并试图接管从迪拜飞往特拉维夫的航班的男子经历了“伊斯兰激进的灌输”。

paras.en: The Flydubai plane plunged more than 17,000ft (5,200m) two hours into its journey on Wednesday, before passengers and crew overpowered the attacker and retook control to land safely.
paras.zh: 周三，这架Flydubai飞机在旅途中坠落了超过17,000英尺（ 5,200米） ，然后乘客和机组人员击败了袭击者并重新夺回了安全降落的控制权。

paras.en: Netanyahu told Fox News that it was looking "very likely" that the attacker, who he said was an Omani national, "was going to down the plane".
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡告诉福克斯新闻，看起来“非常有可能”袭击者，他说是阿曼国民， “要下飞机”。

paras.en: Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) state news agency reports investigations have begun there to determine "whether the incident was linked to any terrorist activity or purpose".
paras.zh: 与此同时，阿联酋国家通讯社报道称，调查已经开始，以确定“该事件是否与任何恐怖活动或目的有关”。

paras.en: The co-pilot is currently being questioned in Saudi Arabia, where the plane made an emergency landing. However, UAE officials say they have jurisdiction over the incident because the aircraft on which the attack took place is registered there and flies under its flag.
paras.zh: 副驾驶目前正在沙特阿拉伯接受讯问，飞机在那里紧急降落。然而，阿联酋官员表示，他们对这一事件拥有管辖权，因为发生袭击的飞机是在那里注册的，并在其旗帜下飞行。

paras.en: Netanyahu told Fox that once the attacker had been subdued and tied up by passengers and crew, he was "calling out to the aircrew 'kill me, kill me', so it's clear he was suicidal - that's not a question".
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡告诉福克斯，一旦袭击者被乘客和机组人员制服和捆绑，他就“呼唤机组人员'杀了我，杀了我' ，所以很明显他是自杀-这不是一个问题”。

paras.en: "And with all the passengers in there, and if you couple that with what I just told you about the Islamist tendencies, that radicalisation that were found in his background, I think... that'll give us a pretty good clue."
paras.zh: “所有乘客都在那里，如果你再加上我刚才告诉你的关于伊斯兰主义倾向，在他的背景下发现的激进化，我认为……那会给我们一个很好的线索。”

paras.en: However, he stressed that he did not want to draw any firm conclusions as to motive yet.
paras.zh: 然而，他强调说，他还不想就动机得出任何确切的结论。

paras.en: Pilots from countries without diplomatic relations with Israel were usually not allowed to fly there, Netanyahu said when asked about how the suspected Omani pilot came to be on the plane.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡在被问及疑似阿曼飞行员是如何登机的时说，来自与以色列没有外交关系的国家的飞行员通常不允许飞往那里。

paras.en: He added: "Obviously there was a loophole here and we're taking care of that among other things... with the full co-operation, I have to say, of the Emirati government, so we're both interested in making sure this doesn't happen again."
paras.zh: 他补充说： “显然这里有一个漏洞，我们正在解决这个问题......我不得不说，与阿联酋政府的全面合作，所以我们都有兴趣确保这种情况不会再次发生。”

paras.en: Oman has not formally established official ties with Israel, unlike the UAE.
paras.zh: 与阿联酋不同，阿曼尚未与以色列正式建立正式关系。

paras.en: The prime minister was also asked earlier on the same network whether there was an indication if Iran was involved, he replied: "It's too early to say".
paras.zh: 总理早些时候也在同一个网络上被问及是否有迹象表明伊朗是否参与其中，他回答说： “现在说还为时过早。”

paras.en: The attacker was arrested in Saudi Arabia and is expected to be transferred to the UAE, Netanyahu said.
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡说，袭击者在沙特阿拉伯被捕，预计将被转移到阿联酋。

paras.en: Both Netanyahu and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the stabbed pilot, Indian national Capt Smit Machchhar was a "hero".
paras.zh: 内塔尼亚胡和印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪（ Narendra Modi ）都表示，这名被刺伤的飞行员，印度国民上尉斯米特·马查尔（ Smit Machchhar ）是一名“

paras.en: India's ambassador to the UAE Deepak Mittal visited Captain Machhar in hospital on Thursday, the Indian Mission confirmed on social media, stating he was "in good health and recovering well".
paras.zh: 印度代表团在社交媒体上证实，印度驻阿联酋大使迪帕克·米塔尔（ Deepak Mittal ）周四在医院拜访了马查尔上尉，称他“身体健康，恢复良好”。

paras.en: Preliminary findings from a separate Israeli investigation into the incident, suggest that the alleged attacker intended to crash the plane, an Israeli security source told BBC Arabic.
paras.zh: 一名以色列安全消息人士告诉英国广播公司阿拉伯语频道，以色列对该事件进行的另一项调查的初步结果表明，据称袭击者打算坠毁这架飞机。

paras.en: The source said the investigation - led by Israel's intelligence agency Mossad - interviewed passengers after they arrived in Tel Aviv to establish what had happened on the plane.
paras.zh: 消息人士称，由以色列情报机构摩萨德牵头的调查在乘客抵达特拉维夫后对他们进行了采访，以确定飞机上发生的事情。

paras.en: Flydubai's flight FZ1073, with more than 170 people on board, took off from Dubai International Airport in the UAE at 03:05 GMT (07:05 local time), en route to Ben Gurion Airport.
paras.zh: Flydubai的FZ1073航班载有170多人，于格林威治标准时间03:05 （当地时间07:05 ）从阿联酋迪拜国际机场起飞，前往本古里安机场。

paras.en: Two hours later, the 17,000ft drop in altitude was reported on the plane tracking website Flightradar24 and minutes later the plane signalled an emergency code.
paras.zh: 两小时后，飞机跟踪网站Flightradar24报告了17,000英尺的高度下降，几分钟后，飞机发出了紧急代码。

paras.en: At about 05:40, the plane - which had briefly entered Jordanian airspace - looped back into Saudi Arabia, where it later started its manual descent, landing safely at Tabuk Airport in the north west of Saudi.
paras.zh: 大约在05:40 ，这架短暂进入约旦领空的飞机环绕回沙特阿拉伯，后来开始手动下降，安全降落在沙特西北部的塔布克机场。

paras.en: Flydubai has since suspended flights between Dubai and Tel Aviv as it carried out its own investigation into the incident.
paras.zh: 此后， Flydubai暂停了迪拜和特拉维夫之间的航班，因为它对这一事件进行了自己的调查。

paras.en: Israel's Transportation Ministry said the suspension aligns with Netanyahu's directive.
paras.zh: 以色列交通部表示，暂停符合内塔尼亚胡的指令。

paras.en: Israeli airlines including El Al, Israir and Arkia said plans were in place to operate rescue flights from Dubai starting on Friday to bring back stranded passengers.
paras.zh: 包括El Al、Israir和Arkia在内的以色列航空公司表示，计划从周五开始从迪拜运营救援航班，以带回滞留的乘客。

paras.en: The Transportation Ministry also said it sent an urgent request to Etihad Airlines to increase the number of flights between Abu Dhabi and Tel Aviv.
paras.zh: 交通部还表示，已向阿提哈德航空公司发出紧急请求，以增加阿布扎比和特拉维夫之间的航班数量。

articles.title: Fires break out at French schools as students protest nationwide

paras.en: Fires have broken out at several schools in France, as students protest by blockading education institutions nationwide over school funding and studying conditions.
paras.zh: 法国的几所学校发生了火灾，学生们通过封锁全国各地的教育机构来抗议学校的资金和学习条件。

paras.en: Blazes were reported at two high schools in Nantes, western France, while another was filmed engulfing the entrance of a school in the northern city of Rouen.
paras.zh: 据报道，法国西部南特的两所高中发生了大火，另一所高中被拍摄到吞没了北部城市鲁昂的一所学校的入口。

paras.en: Students are protesting about a lack of teachers and staff, overcrowded classrooms and run-down buildings. University students joined the demonstrations on Thursday, citing similar demands.
paras.zh: 学生们抗议教师和工作人员短缺、教室过度拥挤和楼房破败。周四，大学生以类似要求为由参加了示威活动。

paras.en: The interior ministry said 1,949 people had been arrested on Thursday, with 305 police officers injured. Prime Minister SÃ©bastien Lecornu held a crisis meeting on Thursday to discuss the unrest.
paras.zh: 内政部表示，周四有1,949人被捕， 305名警察受伤。总理塞巴斯蒂安·勒科努（ Sébastien Lecornu ）周四举行了危机会议，讨论骚乱。

paras.en: The government said afterwards that the student-led demonstrations had descended into "urban violence".
paras.zh: 政府后来表示，学生领导的示威活动已演变为“城市暴力”。

paras.en: Both fires in Nantes spread after a bin was set alight. The blaze at the Nelson Mandela high school, in the city centre, then spread to the front of the building, damaging the entrance hall.
paras.zh: 南特的两场大火在垃圾桶着火后蔓延开来。位于市中心的纳尔逊·曼德拉高中（ Nelson Mandela high school ）的大火随后蔓延到大楼前部，损坏了入口大厅。

paras.en: In the southern city of Marseille, staff at Victor Hugo high school were splashed with petrol as protesters reportedly filled containers.
paras.zh: 在南部城市马赛，维克多·雨果（ Victor Hugo ）高中的工作人员被汽油泼溅，据报道，抗议者在集装箱里装满了汽油。

paras.en: While in the north, a headteacher at Degrugillier high school, in the village of Auchel, was injured in the ear by a wayward firework.
paras.zh: 在北方， Auchel村Degrugillier高中的一名校长被一支任性的烟花炸伤了耳朵。

paras.en: The blockades and protests at French lycÃ©es - for 15-18 year olds and equivalent to sixth forms in the UK or high schools in the US - began last week before spreading to hundreds of schools across the country.
paras.zh: 法国高中（ 15-18岁，相当于英国的六年级学生或美国的高中）的封锁和抗议活动始于上周，随后蔓延到全国数百所学校。

paras.en: At least 30 universities have also reportedly been blockaded, including campuses in Rennes and Paris.
paras.zh: 据报道，至少有30所大学也被封锁，包括雷恩和巴黎的校园。

paras.en: On Thursday, public transport services in Marseille and Strasbourg were halted due vandalism, threats of violence and to hinder protesters from moving around.
paras.zh: 周四，马赛和斯特拉斯堡的公共交通服务因故意破坏、暴力威胁和阻止抗议者四处走动而暂停。

paras.en: Seventeen-year-old Raphael took part in protests outside a school in Strasbourg, where barriers were used to obstruct nearby tram tracks.
paras.zh: 17岁的拉斐尔参加了斯特拉斯堡一所学校外的抗议活动，那里的路障被用来阻挡附近的电车轨道。

paras.en: He voiced his frustration at his school's facilities in an interview with news agency AFP, saying some rooms had leaks and that there were not enough toilets.
paras.zh: 他在接受法新社采访时对学校的设施表示失望，称有些房间漏水，厕所不够用。

paras.en: "The building is falling apart, the cafeteria is too small. There's zero budget, zero resources, not enough supervisors," Raphael said.
paras.zh: “建筑物正在倒塌，自助餐厅太小了。预算为零，资源为零，主管不够，”拉斐尔说。

paras.en: While France's next general election is still months away, the protests and how French authorities are responding to them has been heavily politicised.
paras.zh: 虽然距离法国下次大选还有几个月的时间，但抗议活动以及法国当局如何应对这些抗议活动已被严重政治化。

paras.en: The government and hard-right politicians have blamed the hard left for igniting protests, which are being organised by a union representing lycÃ©e students.
paras.zh: 政府和极右翼政客指责极左派引发了抗议活动，抗议活动由代表lycée学生的工会组织。

paras.en: Bally Bagayoko, the mayor of a Parisian suburb and member of the radical left La France Insoumise (LFI) party defended earlier remarks in which he said violence could be legitimate in some cases - referencing cases in which protesters had allegedly been shot at while not wearing helmets or bulletproof vests.
paras.zh: 巴黎郊区市长、激进左翼政党La France Insoumise （ LFI ）成员Bally Bagayoko为早些时候的言论辩护，他说，在某些情况下，暴力行为可能是合法的--他提到了据称抗议者在没有戴头盔或防弹背心的情况下遭到枪击的案件。

paras.en: LFI leader and presidential candidate Jean-Luc MÃ©lenchon, meanwhile, stressed he was in favour of non-violent protests, while arguing that blaming the left would not solve the issues motivating the demonstrations.
paras.zh: 与此同时， LFI领导人兼总统候选人让-吕克·梅朗雄（ Jean-Luc Mélenchon ）强调，他赞成非暴力抗议，同时认为指责左派并不能解决引发示威活动的问题。

paras.en: Earlier, leader of the hard-right National Rally Marine Le Pen said: "This is no longer about high school student protests. It is about riots organized by professionals and overseen by deputies from La France Insoumise."
paras.zh: 早些时候，极右翼全国集会领导人马琳·勒庞（ Marine Le Pen ）说： “这不再是高中生抗议活动。这是关于由专业人士组织并由La France Insoumise的代表监督的骚乱。”

paras.en: The presidential candidate called for a new anti-rioting law to be passed.
paras.zh: 这位总统候选人呼吁通过一项新的反暴乱法。

paras.en: Left-wing mayor of Marseille BenoÃ®t Payan condemned the "unacceptable violence" in his city.
paras.zh: 马赛的左翼市长贝诺·帕扬（ Benoót Payan ）谴责了该市“不可接受的暴力”。

paras.en: While young people were "legitimately concerned" about their future and public services, they must express themselves in a calm fashion, he said.
paras.zh: 他说，虽然年轻人“理所当然地关心”他们的未来和公共服务，但他们必须以平静的方式表达自己。

paras.en: Eric Ciotti, the Republicans mayor of Nice, said the parents of those found to have damaged school property should be made to pay for the repairs.
paras.zh: 尼斯共和党市长埃里克·奇奥蒂（ Eric Ciotti ）表示，应该让那些被发现损坏学校财产的人的父母支付维修费用。

articles.title: The Avalanches Set 2027 Tour of Australia
articles.author: Lars Brandle

paras.en: The Avalanches will rumble down under in early 2027 for a live tour that includes a date at the Sydney Opera House Forecourt.
paras.zh: Avalanches 乐队将于 2​​027 年初隆隆作响，进行现场巡演，其中包括在悉尼歌剧院前院举行的演出。

paras.en: Led by Robbie Chater, Tony Di Blasi and Andy Szekeres, the electronic music pioneers will play six concerts across Australia next February and March.
paras.zh: 在 Robbie Chater、Tony Di Blasi 和 Andy Szekeres 的带领下，电子音乐先驱们将于明年二月和三月在澳大利亚举办六场音乐会。

paras.en: Presented by Takumi, the jaunt gets underway with two shows at Perth Festival, then heads east to Adelaide’s Hindley St Music Hall; the group’s hometown, Melbourne, for Live At The Gardens; On The Banks in Brisbane, and wraps up at the iconic Sydney Opera House.
paras.zh: 在 Takumi 的主持下，这次旅行在珀斯音乐节上进行了两场演出，然后向东前往阿德莱德的 Hindley St 音乐厅；乐队的家乡墨尔本，Live At The Gardens；在布里斯班的河岸上，最后在标志性的悉尼歌剧院结束。

paras.en: “The chaotic virtuosity and charm of The Avalanches have brought unmatched joy to ears and feet around the world for more than 25 years,” remarks Sydney Opera House head of contemporary music Ben Marshall. “After hosting them at Vivid LIVE in the Studio in 2011 and on the Northern Broadwalk in 2017, it’s a thrill to finally hand them the keys to the Sydney Opera House Forecourt.”
paras.zh: “25 年来，《雪崩》混乱的精湛技艺和魅力为世界各地的耳朵和脚带来了无与伦比的欢乐，”悉尼歌剧院当代音乐总监本·马歇尔 (Ben Marshall) 说道。 “继 2011 年在工作室 Vivid LIVE 和 2017 年在北大道 (Northern Broadwalk) 接待他们之后，最终将悉尼歌剧院前院的钥匙交给他们真是令人兴奋。”

paras.en: From the very start, The Avalanches “have continually reconstructed the DNA of electronic music with a generous cast of brilliantly curated, visionary guests,” Marshall enthuses. “Experiencing their kaleidoscopic, deeply human storytelling on the grandest stage our city can offer will be an extraordinary summer moment – and a hell of a lot of fun.”
paras.zh: 马歇尔兴奋地说，从一开始，雪崩乐队就“不断重建电子音乐的 DNA，拥有大量精心策划、富有远见的嘉宾”。 “在我们城市所能提供的最宏伟的舞台上体验他们千变万化、深刻的人性化故事，将是一个非凡的夏日时刻——而且充满乐趣。”

paras.en: Joining The Avalanches on those final east coast shows (Melbourne, Brisbane, Sydney) is HAAi, the Australia-born, London-based electronic music artist, whose new 10-track collection, DIGITiSE, drops Oct. 9 via Mute Records.
paras.zh: 出生于澳大利亚、现居伦敦的电子音乐艺术家 HAAi 将与 The Avalanches 一起参加东海岸最后的演出（墨尔本、布里斯班、悉尼），他的全新 10 首曲目合集 DIGITiSE 将于 10 月 9 日通过 Mute Records 发售。

paras.en: The Avalanches are gearing up for the release of their own, fourth studio album, No Bad Memories (via Modular Recordings), due out Oct. 16.
paras.zh: Avalanches 正在准备发行他们自己的第四张录音室专辑《No Bad Memories》（通过 Modular Recordings），将于 10 月 16 日发行。

paras.en: With their debut 2000 album Since I Left You, The Avalanches created an instant classic. Its genius, slivers of thousands of vinyl samples from the likes of Françoise Hardy, Sérgio Mendes, Raekwon, Wayne and Shuster, and even Madonna, painstakingly, surgically woven into a musical patchwork.
paras.zh: The Avalanches 于 2000 年凭借首张专辑《Since I Left You》创造了经典。它的天才之处在于，将来自 Françoise Hardy、Sérgio Mendes、Raekwon、Wayne 和 Shuster，甚至 Madonna 等人的数千张黑胶唱片样本片段，精心地、外科手术般地编织成音乐拼凑而成。

paras.en: The result, which included the title track and “Frontier Psychiatrist,” was a collection that was both timeless, and immediate. Or, as a statement from the band’s reps suggests, “a global footprint for collaborative sampology in the 21st century.”
paras.zh: 结果，包括主打歌和“Frontier Psychiatrist”，是一个既永恒又直接的集合。或者，正如乐队代表的一份声明所暗示的那样，“21 世纪合作萨姆学的全球足迹。”

paras.en: Its followup was 16 years in the making. Many thought it would never see the light of day. When it did arrive, Wildflower immediately went to No. 1 on the ARIA Albums Chart. A third album travelled at comparative warp-speed in 2020, We Will Always Love You, and later scooped the coveted Australian Music Prize, for the best album of the year.
paras.zh: 其后续作品的制作耗时16年。许多人认为它永远不会见到曙光。当它到达时，《Wildflower》立即在 ARIA 专辑排行榜上名列第一。 2020 年，第三张专辑《We Will Always Love You》以相对惊人的速度发行，随后荣获了令人垂涎的澳大利亚音乐奖年度最佳专辑。

paras.en: The new project, Chater explains, began with “rhythmic experiments using the sonic leftovers and hallmarks of the technologies we grew up with,” with recordings of hard drives, computer hardware and forgotten technologies becoming part of the album’s sonic palette.
paras.zh: 查特解释说，这个新项目始于“利用我们成长过程中所留下的声音和技术特征进行节奏实验”，硬盘、计算机硬件和被遗忘的技术的录音成为专辑声音调色板的一部分。

paras.en: No Bad Memories includes the previously released cuts “Together” with Nikki Nair, Jessy Lanza and Prentiss; “Every Single Weekend” with Jamie xx; “Blue Shadows” with Karen O; “Can’t Get Over Losing You” with Portraits of Tracy; and most recently “Far Away” with John Glacier and Khadija Al Hanafi.
paras.zh: 《No Bad Memories》包括之前与 Nikki Nair、Jessy Lanza 和 Prentiss 一起发布的剪辑版《Together》；与 Jamie xx 合作的《Every Single Weekend》；与凯伦·欧 (Karen O) 合作的《蓝色阴影》； 《无法忘记失去你》与特蕾西的肖像；以及最近与 John Glacier 和 Khadija Al Hanafi 合作的《Far Away》。

paras.en: The general onsale for the 2027 Australia tour starts Tuesday, Oct. 6 at 9am local time. Click here for tickets and information. The artist pre-sale opens earlier.
paras.zh: 2027 年澳大利亚巡演的全面预售将于当地时间 10 月 6 日星期二上午 9 点开始。单击此处获取门票和信息。艺术家预售提前开始。

paras.en: Before heading home, The Avalanches will complete a run of dates across Continental Europe and the United Kingdom, including a sold-out show Nov. 27 at The Roundhouse in London.
